graph.method: function-level static graph over the exact candidate DSOs: nm-defined functions, objdump direct call edges, address-taken code references, function pointers in .data.rel.ro/.data/.rodata, .init_array/.fini_array roots; unresolved indirect calls admit all address-taken functions (conservative upper bound)
graph.upper_bound_rule: once any reachable function performs an unresolved indirect call, every function whose address is materialised anywhere in the candidate DSOs is admitted; the upper bound is the reachable set used for adjudication

reachable_export_symbols.note: candidate DSO exports reached by the graph, including the 12 consumer imports; the consumer-imported set is in symbol_evidence

special_edges.note: each listed class was checked against the reachable set of the exact candidate code; an empty list is an observed absence on this closure, not an assumption.  A reachable dynamic name lookup would be an unmodelled edge class because the static graph cannot resolve names

unmapped_crate_functions.note: crate-namespace functions with no module-path mapping; they are a coverage limit of the demangler, not a claim of unreachability

observed_trace.note: no observed execution trace was supplied; the closure is the static upper bound alone

limits: inlined callees have no out-of-line function node; their code is attributed to the caller, so a source file whose only contribution is inlined has no node of its own
unresolved indirect calls are not resolved per call site; the bound admits the global address-taken set instead of guessing a target
a dynamic trace proves execution, not unreachability, and never narrowed this graph
function-level reachability is not a proof that a site is safe; it bounds which obligations apply
